verdicts.reason: Every cited line opened and matched verbatim. §1t99s0§.as:3094 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4;', :3105 '* (1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1)', :3116 '* (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4423s0§ * 0.1)' with :3117-3119 'if(this.§1t4417s0§ < 100){this.§1t4417s0§ = 100;}'. I verified the two links the finding only asserted. (a) §1t4420s0§ really is baseSlashLength: :105 declares it =10, :194 assigns it from param10, and §1t1523s0§.as:2268 passes §1t9592s0§() in argument slot 10 of the initPlayer twin — the android line MCSPlayer.as:182/:193 + StatsManager.as:1834 has the same slot named baseSlashLength. (b) §1t9593s0§ at :2344-2348 is verbatim 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));' and its android twin getBaseSlashLengthVal is character-for-character identical with the obfuscated ids resolved as STAT_DAN and STAT_SPEED, including the x1.5 BUFF_SPEED step — so the finding's stat identifications are right, not guessed. (c) the length-budget semantics do not even need the android cite it gives: the WEB twin §1t1541s0§.as:51 carries the same unobfuscated 'internal static var maxDistance:int = 200;' and :106 is the setter called from §1t99s0§.as:3158. Arithmetic checks: dan 0 gives base 120 (SPD 0) rising asymptotically to 210, so Light 168-294, Balanced 120-252, Heavy max(100, 60-189), +5 px asymptote per dan. RR:190 blocker (1) 'measure blade-FX tip-to-body span ... from footage' is therefore a dead close-path — the value is computed in the target build. Two residual notes that do NOT refute: the finding's ranges take mastery 10 (settled below), and it omits the INJURED debuff at §1t99s0§.as:223 'this.§1t4420s0§ *= 0.5;' which halves every stance's reach. Incompleteness, not error.

All four quoted lines are verbatim at the lines given: :3344 'var _loc6_:Boolean = ... < 1 + (_loc2_ + 10) * 3;', :3422 '§1t1523s0§.§1t9713s0§(§1t1523s0§.§1t9408s0§,3);', :3457 '_loc1_ += (§1t1523s0§.§1t9714s0§(§1t1523s0§.§1t9408s0§) - 1) / 3;', :3461 '_loc2_ = (§1t1523s0§.getLevel() - 1) * 3;'. The one thing the finding leaves implicit — that _loc2_ at :3340 is the LEVEL — I checked independently: the android twin of the identical six-line visibility block reads 'var charlevel:int = StatsManager.getStat(StatsManager.STAT_LEVEL);' at InventoryUI.as:2406 followed by the same six .visible assignments at :2407-2412, so §1t9411s0§ = STAT_LEVEL (=10, StatsManager.as:190). The arithmetic then holds exactly: ATK base 1, step 3, cap 1+(80+10)*3 = 271 under a strict '<', so the ladder 1,4,...,268 grants once more and lands on 271; cost (271-1)/3 = 90 of the (80-1)*3 = 237 budget, 147 to spare. Both halves of the RR:201 parenthetical fall — the budget does NOT make 271 impossible in one stat, and the cap is not gear-inclusive either, since :3344 tests §1t9714s0§ (base getStat) while the gear bonus §1t7358s0§ is added separately at §1t1523s0§.as:2268. As a bonus the same block is a shipped anti-cheat spend audit (:3454-3462 with the warning at :3464), exactly as the finding says.

Verbatim at the lines cited: §1t68s0§.as:863 '§1t406s0§.instance.§1t6488s0§.§1t5846s0§(1 * _loc8_);' and :867 '...§1t5846s0§(5 * _loc8_);', android NPC.as:839 'addLootCoins(1 * qty);' / :843 'addLootCoins(5 * qty);', with types 2/3/else at :869-879 handing to quest item, level-scaled random item and literal item id. I also opened the twenty lines the finding did not quote, which are what actually kill the '=8 seed': :820-828 walk 'this.reward.loot', reading type, qty and 'chance' per entry and rolling 'if(_loc6_ == 100 || Math.random() * 100 < _loc6_)'. So coins per kill in v0.717 is a per-NPC rolled loot table paying 1x or 5x qty, not a constant. The finding also asserts the XP half of RR:215 blocker (1) is already dead; I did not take that on trust and checked — NPC.as:218 'this.xp = this.level * 2 + 20;' and :166 'public static function calcXP(playerLevel:int, mobLevel:int, xp:int, elite:Boolean)' with the level-difference scaling at :179/:183, consumed at :863 addLootXP(calcXP(...)). Both halves of the blocker do fall together. Caveat recorded, not held against it: the coins half is proven WEB-side, the XP formula I verified is android v0.682.

The core claim is exactly right and it is the strongest kind of evidence this lane can get — WEB build, in code, literals. §1t401s0§.as:1087 'cost = 5000;'; :1105 'weaponlevel = weapon.getLevel();' with :1106-1108 forcing itemID 13022 to level 59; :1110/:1112/:1120 demand-and-spend stat 20064 under level 30, :1122/:1124/:1132 stat 20065 under 60, :1134/:1136/:1144 stat 20066 otherwise; then :1146 '§1t1523s0§.§1t9619s0§(-cost);' and :1147 'weapon.uses = 0;'. itemdata.xml gives <id>20064</id> at :10420, 20065 at :10429, 20066 at :10438, and strings.json resolves 4241/4242/4243 to 'Silver Ore' / 'Titanium Ore' / 'Uncut Diamond' — I read all three back from the index. RR:80's 'Reinforce 5000c+1 silver ore' is therefore an under-specification that falls, and the S0-3 android hedge is genuinely discharged here because the tier logic is web-side. ONE nit, flagged and not fatal: the quote field says "itemdata.xml:10420 '<id>20064</id>' with :10421 '<name>4241</name>'" — :10421 is actually '<type>12</type>' and <name>4241</name> sits at :10422. The declared cite range 10418-10442 does contain the right line and the id->name mapping is correct, so this is an off-by-one inside a supporting detail, not a mis-cite that changes anything. Fix the line number when the row is written into the ledger.

The mechanism the finding describes is real and I reproduced the grep it rests on. §1t7785s0§.as:162 is verbatim 'public function §1t7835s0§(param1:String, param2:Array, param3:int, param4:int = 6, param5:int = 6) : *' and :176-177 are 'this.ht = param4;' / 'this.wt = param5;' — no literal 6 anywhere in the web class, exactly as claimed. grep for §1t7835s0§ across the whole payload returns precisely two hits, the declaration itself and §1t6483s0§.as:588 'this.§1t8003s0§.§1t7835s0§(param1,param3,param4);' — three arguments, so both dimension defaults are taken and ht = wt = 6 in v0.717. The structural-twin argument also survives inspection: the loops at :200-204 bound by param5/param4 sit exactly where WarHexUI.as:199-202 bound by wt/ht do, and the pitch/origin match line-for-line (§1t7785s0§.as:208-209 '_loc12_.x = 90 + _loc13_ * 55;' / '.y = 92 + _loc23_ * 55;' vs WarHexUI.as:206-207 'warTerrain.x = 90 + i * 55;' / 'warTerrain.y = 92 + j * 55;'). Android hardcodes 'this.ht = 6;' / 'this.wt = 6;' at :175-176 and those are indeed its only two assignments (every other ht/wt hit is a read). RR:245 blocker (2) does change — with the honest scope the finding itself states: the BOARD half is closed at the target build; per-hex ownership/exit state still arrives from territoryData (:211 / WarHexUI.as:209), so the edit is 'board settled, live state feed still server-side', not deletion of the blocker.

Quotes verbatim: WarHexUI.as:195 'var zeronodex:int = (this.mapid >> 12 & 0x0FFF) * 6;', :196 'var zeronodey:int = (this.mapid & 0x0FFF) * 6;', :197 'var zeronodeid:int = zeronodex << 12 | zeronodey;', :208 'nodeid = NodeGenerator.instance.getShiftedNodeId(zeronodeid,i,j);'. The web twin carries the identical transform at §1t7785s0§.as:196-198 with the shift call at :210. The step the finding asserts but does not open, I opened: NodeGenerator.as:1780-1789 'var xpart:int = (currentNodeID >> 12 & 0x0FFF) + shiftX; var ypart:int = (currentNodeID & 0x0FFF) + shiftY; ... return xpart << 12 | ypart;' — which makes the packed id exactly (sectorX*6 + i) << 12 | (sectorY*6 + j), the formula the finding states. That a node is a ROOM is confirmed by the consumer at :209/:1570 'public function getRoomBG(nodeid:int)'. So a territory occupies a 6-by-6 block of room node ids and the war hex grid is the room grid in the same coordinate space. RR:225 blocker (5) 'sector<->room mapping rule (town=fixed sector vs wilderness=one-screen-per-sector)' falls: it is 36 rooms per sector, uniformly, not one screen per sector. Standing caveat: both derivations are android v0.682 for the loop, but the web transform at §1t7785s0§.as:196-198 is byte-equivalent, so the parity hole here is narrow.

Verbatim at the lines given: :3262 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4421s0§ * 0.1);', :3265 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * (1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1);', :3270 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;' (heavy flat, shared by three cases), :3116 heavy reach on the same 0.5+0.04m shape. The field identifications are sound — :107/:109/:111 declare §1t4421s0§/§1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§ in the same slot order the android twin names lightMastery/balancedMastery/heavyMastery. Arithmetic confirmed: 0.5+0.04m is 0.86 at m=9 and 0.90 only at m=10; 1+0.02m is 1.18 at m=9 and 1.20 only at m=10. RR:155's 'MASTERY-9 CEILING' label cannot stand beside these formulas either way, so the overturn holds. I then went one step past the finding, which honestly declared the mastery cap STILL_UNHELD from its own file: skilldata.xml skill 1000 (:4), 1001 (:83) and 1002 (:162) each carry exactly ten <level> rows with <value> 1..10, so the scale is 1-10 and the fork resolves to the FIRST horn — the ceilings 0.9/1.2 are real and the ledger's '-9' label is simply off by one. Recorded as a new finding, together with the floor: web §1t1523s0§.as:1058-1060 seeds the three masteries at value 1, not 0.

new_findings.build: web v0.717 (skilldata.xml row counts are android-sourced per C2; the formulas and the seed value are web)
new_findings.text: Resolves the fork that s27b/stance-ceilings-are-mastery-10-not-mastery-9 correctly left open, and adds a second error in the same ledger sentence. (a) THE CAP IS 10: skilldata.xml skills 1000/1001/1002 (:4, :83, :162 — the three passive stance masteries fed to initPlayer as getStat(1000/1001/1002)) each have exactly ten <level> rows valued 1..10. So the web formulas 0.5+0.04m and 1+0.02m do reach 0.90 and 1.20, at m=10, and RR:155's 'MASTERY-9' label is an off-by-one rather than an unreachable ceiling. (b) THE FLOOR IS 1, NOT 0: the web build seeds all three masteries at value 1 (§1t1523s0§.as:1058-1060, mirrored at :2586-2588 for the second init path), so a fresh character is at m=1, not m=0. RR:155-156's 'A level-1 Shugyosha does Light x0.5 / Balanced x1.0 ... Heavy's reach also scales x0.5' is therefore wrong at both ends: the real floors are Light x0.54, Balanced x1.02 and heavy reach x0.54, and the real ceilings are x0.9 / x1.2 / x0.9 at m=10. Ship the two formulas with the domain m in [1,10]; do not ship the triple.
new_findings.ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.** A level-1 Shugyosha does Light ×0.5 / Balanced ×1.0 / Heavy ×1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's *reach* also scales ×0.5→×0.9.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters: RR:155-156 needs both numbers replaced, not just the '-9' label. STANCE_DMG_LIGHT(m) = 0.5 + 0.04m, STANCE_DMG_BALANCED(m) = 1 + 0.02m, STANCE_DMG_HEAVY = 1.4 flat, STANCE_REACH_HEAVY(m) = 0.5 + 0.04m, m in [1,10] seeded at 1. Kills the 'decide-and-flag: the build targets mastery-9' escape hatch — there is a curve and it is two lines of code.

new_findings.text: Found while auditing the reach-cap finding, which builds the whole stage-px model out of baseSlashLength and never mentions that one status effect halves it. Immediately after the buff chain at §1t99s0§.as:215-218, the web build's player init runs 'else if(§1t1523s0§.§1t9725s0§(§1t1523s0§.§1t9463s0§))' and applies THREE halvings at :221-223 — minDamage, defense and baseSlashLength. The android twin at MCSPlayer.as:218-223 names the branch 'StatsManager.hasBuff(StatsManager.BUFF_INJURED)', which is what identifies the obfuscated §1t9463s0§. Consequence for the ledger row being written from the reach finding: INJURED is a x0.5 multiplier on baseSlashLength, so it scales every stance's reach at once — Light drops to 84-147 px, Balanced to 60-126, Heavy to the 100 floor for its whole range. It is applied at init, before the stance branch at :3094/:3105/:3116 reads the field, so it composes multiplicatively and the Heavy floor of 100 still clamps last. Also note it is exclusive with the speed buff branch (else-if), which is the same field the SPD x1.5 feeds through.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: whatever REACH config const comes out of blocker (1) must carry an INJURED x0.5 modifier on baseSlashLength, not on the per-stance multiplier. Same line also gives free CONTRACT values for the injured DMG and DEF penalties (both x0.5), which the combat-core and enemies-ai rows do not have.
